package_info.package_manager: N/A (malware binary, not a package manager ecosystem)
package_info.why_malicious: Mozart is a Windows backdoor malware that establishes covert command-and-control (C&C) communication with attacker infrastructure by abusing DNS TXT records, enabling remote command execution and data exfiltration while evading traditional network monitoring.

malicious_snippets.code_snippet: The backdoor uses DNS TXT records to communicate with its C&C server, sending and receiving commands and data via DNS queries and responses.
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, the code crafts DNS TXT record queries to attacker-controlled domains, encodes commands or data in the DNS payload, and parses TXT record responses to receive instructions, enabling covert remote command execution and data exfiltration.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: The use of DNS TXT records for command-and-control is a known evasion technique, as DNS traffic is often permitted and less scrutinized than HTTP/S. The malware's ability to parse and execute commands received via DNS responses is highly indicative of malicious intent.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Legitimate software does not use DNS TXT records to receive and execute remote commands or exfiltrate data; DNS is typically used only for domain name resolution or, in rare cases, for configuration retrieval, not for establishing a C&C channel.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Some legitimate applications may use DNS TXT records for service discovery or configuration (e.g., SPF records, cloud service bootstrapping), but they do not parse and execute arbitrary commands or transfer sensitive data via DNS.
key_indicators: High volume of DNS TXT queries to domains not associated with legitimate services
DNS payloads containing encoded or encrypted data
Process activity correlating with DNS responses (e.g., execution of commands received via DNS)
Absence of standard HTTP/S C&C traffic despite ongoing remote control activity

attack_chain.action: Initial infection occurs via a phishing email that delivers the Mozart backdoor malware binary to the target system.
attack_chain.leads_to: The Mozart backdoor is installed and executed on the victim's machine.

attack_chain.action: Upon execution, the backdoor establishes a covert C&C channel using DNS TXT records to communicate with attacker-controlled domains.
attack_chain.leads_to: The attacker can remotely send commands and receive data from the infected system, maintaining persistent control.

behavioral_signatures: Malware establishing command-and-control via DNS TXT record queries and responses
Unusual or high-frequency DNS TXT queries to external or unrecognized domains
Execution of system commands or scripts in response to DNS TXT record data
file_indicators: Presence of unknown or suspicious binaries named mozart.exe or similar
Artifacts of phishing email delivery (e.g., email attachments or links leading to malware download)
network_indicators: Frequent DNS TXT queries to attacker-controlled or non-standard domains
DNS traffic with large or anomalous TXT record payloads containing encoded or encrypted data
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Monitor DNS traffic for excessive or anomalous TXT record queries, especially to domains not associated with legitimate business services. Correlate these queries with endpoint process activity to identify binaries (such as mozart.exe) making such requests. Flag any execution of commands or scripts where the input is sourced from DNS TXT record responses. Investigate the presence of suspicious binaries and phishing email artifacts on endpoints.
